sentences.text: At the outset, it is pertinent to mention that the Trial Court committed an error in convicting the appellant/accused No.1 for both the offences under Section 304(B) IPC as well as Section 302 of IPC.

If the Trial Court was of the opinion that, it was a case of 302 IPC, based on the evidence and material on the record, then question of convicting the accused again for the offence punishable under Section 304(B) of IPC would not arise.

Similarly, if there is no evidence to establish the charge under Section 302 IPC, and if there was evidence to show that the deceased was subjected to cruelty for the purpose of dowry soon before her death, the Trial Court would be justified in convicting the accused for the offence under Section 304(B) of IPC.
8.
We are mindful to the fact that the case against accused Nos.2 to 4 has been split up and they are not sent for trial along with the appellant/accused No.1.

However, the evidence adduced by the prosecution being one and the same against all the NC: 2026:KHC-D:1371-DB HC-KAR accused, we may have to refer to the testimony of the prosecution witnesses, insofar as the appellant, i.e.,
accused No.1 is concerned.

Hence, we are making it clear that we are not expressing any opinion,
insofar as the evidence as against accused Nos.2 to 4 are concerned.

9. It is the specific case of the prosecution that the marriage of deceased Chandini was performed with accused No.1 on 11.04.2010 and she died an unnatural death on 26.07.2015, which is within 7 years from the date of her marriage.
The defence has not seriously disputed the relationship or the date of death.
However, the prime contention raised by the learned counsel for the appellant is that the deceased died on account of stove burst and not on account of any act committed by the accused.
To buttress the said argument, the learned counsel would draw the attention of the Court to Ex.P.2 i.e., the complaint lodged by the brother of the deceased/PW.1.

He would contend that as per Ex.P.2,
NC: 2026:KHC-D:1371-DB HC-KAR one Khaja Pasha Kavaluru (PW.9) informed the complainant over the phone that his sister Chandini has sustained burn injuries due to stove burst and admitted to the District Hospital for treatment.

He would therefore contend that, as per the earliest information received by PW.2, it is evident that the victim sustained burn injuries on account of stove burst and therefore, the case of the prosecution that it was the accused who set her on fire after pouring kerosene or she died on account of cruelty meted to her soon before her death, consequent to the demand of dowry by the accused etc. are false.
10.
Insofar as the deceased succumbing to the burn injuries is concerned, the prosecution has relied on the post-mortem report/Ex.P.11 as well as the inquest report/Ex.P.6.

The first informant i.e.,
PW.1, is a resident of Kukanur.
The deceased was a residing along with the accused in her matrimonial home situated in Koppal.

In Ex.P.2 it is stated that on 23.07.2015 at NC:

informed over phone that the victim has sustained burn injuries due to stove burst and admitted to District Hospital.

He has further stated that when he enquired with Khaja Pasha of Koppal, he informed him that on 23.07.2015 at about 01.30 p.m., all the accused poured kerosene on the deceased and set her on fire.

He conducted the spot mahazar/Ex.P.3 and handed over the investigation to PW.20, who has deposed that he received the M.L.C. from KIMS, Hubballi regarding the death of Chandini on 26.07.2015 at about 12.30 a.m. and on the same day, he requested the Tahasildar to conduct the inquest panchanama.

He noticed burn injuries all over the body except the stomach, private part and on back of - 11 - NC: 2026:KHC-D:1371-DB HC-KAR the head and on both the feet.

The learned counsel for the appellant contended that since the said Khadar Pasha is not examined by the prosecution, an adverse inference has to be drawn that the prosecution has intentionally withheld the said witness.

However, what is relevant to - 13 - NC: 2026:KHC-D:1371-DB HC-KAR be seen is that the incident has taken place inside the four walls of the house i.e. the matrimonial home of the deceased, wherein the evidence adduced by the prosecution goes to show that the accused was also residing.

16. The contention of the learned counsel for the appellant that the prosecution has tried to suppress the fact of stove bust and non-examination of Khadar Pasha (CW.18) is fatal to the prosecution case cannot be accepted.

17. Even according to the defence, the accused/appellant sustained burn injuries to his hands.
The defence has tried to contend that the said burn injuries were sustained by him while he was trying to save the victim, when she sustained burns due to stove bust.

As we have already held that there was no evidence of stove burst and the contention of the learned counsel for the appellant cannot be accepted, at the same time, the fact of accused sustaining burn - 15 - NC: 2026:KHC-D:1371-DB HC-KAR injuries would go to show that, he was present in the house at the time of incident.

sentences.text: In the cross-examination, it is elicited from PW.15 that the injuries noticed in Ex.P.15 could be caused, when a person tries to save someone who has suffered burns.

19. In the case on hand, accused while recording his statement under Section 313 Cr.P.C. has denied all the incriminating evidence appeared against him, except admitting taking treatment from the doctor for the burn injury sustained by him.
He has not stated that the - 16 - NC: 2026:KHC-D:1371-DB HC-KAR deceased sustained burn injuries due to stove burst and he sustained injuries while trying to save the deceased.
He being present in the house, no efforts were made to explain the fact which was within his special knowledge.
As we see from the evidence and material on record, the case of the defence that the deceased sustained burn injuries on account of stove burst is not supported by any convincing evidence.
From the evidence of P.W.6, it can be gathered that the story of stove burst was introduced by accused themselves.

She has stated that she was informed by Khaja Pasha that when he went to the hospital, Sajjad Sab i.e., the father in law of the deceased told him that the deceased sustained burn injuries due to stove burst.
However, there is no evidence to show that the deceased caught fire and sustained burn injuries due to stove burst.
On the other hand, P.W.13, who conducted the spot mahazar has categorically stated that there was no stove or any such evidence available when the mahazar was conducted.

Hence, we are of the firm view that the deceased sustained burn injuries not accidentally and not on account of stove burst.

20. Having held that it is not a case of stove burst and deceased has not sustained accidental burn injuries, the next question that would arise is as to 'whether the prosecution has proved the charge under Section 302 of IPC'?
21.
The learned Additional SPP contended that the deceased and accused No.1 were residing in the same house.

The deceased sustained burn injuries under suspicious circumstances and the fact that the accused also sustained burn injuries and his abscondence would establish the charge against him under Section 302 of IPC.
22.

He further contended that the accused has not given any explanation about him sustaining injuries and also as to what happened on the date of incident - 18 - NC: 2026:KHC-D:1371-DB HC-KAR and how the deceased sustained burn injuries.

He further contended that P.W.6 has categorically stated that when she went to the Hospital, the deceased was in a condition to speak and she informed her that the accused has poured kerosene and set fire, for Sri. 7 not bringing additional dowry.

He has therefore, contended that the prosecution has proved the charge framed against the accused under Section 302 of IPC.
23.
The incident took place on 23.07.2015 between 01.30 to 01.40 p.m.
As per prosecution, the victim was immediately shifted to Koppal Government Hospital and from there, she was shifted to KIMS Hospital, Hubballi.
She succumbed to the injuries after three days i.e., on 26.07.2015 in the early hours.
The prosecution has not marked any documents relating to Koppal Government Hospital, to show that the victim was in a condition to speak.

Further, as could be seen from the medical evidence of P.W.16 and P.W.17, the doctors working at KIMS, Hubballi, the victim was not in - 19 - NC: 2026:KHC-D:1371-DB HC-KAR a fit condition to give any statement.

24. P.W.18 is the Police constable, who went to KIMS Hospital, Hubballi on 01.10.2015 on the direction of the Dy.S.P., Koppal to verify the condition of the victim.
He has stated that when he met the doctors and enquired about the condition of the patient, he was informed that she is not in a fit condition to give any statement.

25. Coming to the evidence of P.W.6, mother of the victim, her deposition that, when she enquired,
victim informed that the accused has poured kerosene and set fire on her is not corroborated by any other evidence including evidence of the first informant, brother of the deceased.

On the other hand,
there is sufficient material to show that the victim was - 20 - NC: 2026:KHC-D:1371-DB HC-KAR unconscious at the time of admission at KIMS Hospital,
Hubballi and she was not in a position to give any statement.
The evidence of P.W.6, creates doubt in the mind of the Court and does not inspire the confidence of the Court, hence, cannot be accepted without any corroboration.
26. The accused and the deceased were alone living in the house where the incident took place.
The accused also sustained burn injuries, which confirms about his presence in the house.
Accused took treatment for the burn injuries from P.W.15, who issued the wound certificate marked as Ex.P15.
He has stated that accused was brought by his brother on 26.07.2015 at about 12.05 noon.

However,
merely because he has also sustained burn injuries, it will not lead to draw an inference that he,
poured kerosene on the deceased and set fire to her, without any other convincing evidence placed on record.

sentences.text: Learned Additional S.P.P would contend that P.W.8, a resident of Koppal, a neighbour has deposed that accused was always quarreling with the deceased and he has stated that it is the accused who have poured kerosene and set fire to her.
He contended that the said witness has seen appellant holding the deceased and at that time, the accused had sustained burn injuries.
28. A perusal of the evidence of P.W.8 does not indicate that, he was an eye witness to the incident.
He has spoken about the earlier quarrel and according to him, a quarrel took place in the house of the accused.
By the time he saw, the deceased had already sustained burn injuries.
Accused No.1 was holding the hand of the victim and he had also sustained burn injuries.
29. Evidence of P.W.8 is not helpful to the prosecution to prove the charge under Section 302 of IPC.
Further, merely because the accused was absconding from the spot after the incident will also not - 22 - NC: 2026:KHC-D:1371-DB HC-KAR lead to draw an inference that he has committed the murder.

The suspicion cannot take the place of proof, however grave.
30.
To prove the charge under Section 4 of D.P. Act, 498(A) and 304(B) of IPC, the prosecution is mainly relying on the evidence of P.Ws.1, 5 to 10.

In Ex.P2, it is stated that at the time of marriage,
cash of Rs.10,000/- and 4 tolas of gold was given to the accused and the couple have resided together happily for about two years.
Even from the evidence of P.W.1, P.W.5 and P.W.6, we find that a cash of Rs.10,000/- and 4 tolas of gold was given to the accused.
However, it is not stated that the said cash and gold was demanded by the accused.
Insofar as the payment made subsequently to the tune of Rs.40,000/- to Rs.50,000/-, there is no mention about the said demand in Ex.P2.
The trial Court has found inconsistency about the said additional dowry given to the accused, after the marriage.
Even - 23 - NC: 2026:KHC-D:1371-DB HC-KAR otherwise, the trial Court has acquitted the accused of the charge framed under Section 3 of the D.P. Act.
31. P.W.1 in his evidence has stated that in the year 2013, he got married and at that time, they had been to Koppal to call his sister for the marriage.
However, the accused refused to send her, telling that they will send her, only if gold was given.
At that time, they expressed that they are not able to give gold, but they will give 2 acres of land.
Accused No.1 demanded that the land should be registered in his name.
The said demand made particularly by accused No.1 is also spoken by other witnesses-PWs.5, 6 and 7.
The witnesses have even spoken about an earlier incident, wherein the accused caused burn injuries to the leg of the deceased.
The cruelty meted to the deceased is consistently spoken by the witnesses.

sentences.text: Even though there was no complaint or case registered for causing burn injuries to the leg of deceased, the said fact has been spoken by the - 24 - NC: 2026:KHC-D:1371-DB HC-KAR witnesses including P.W.7, the Jamath President.
There is nothing elicited in the cross-examination of the witnesses to disbelieve the same.

From the evidence of the above witnesses, we have no hesitation to hold that the appellant/accused No.1, two years after the marriage, was harassing the deceased and subjecting her to cruelty making unlawful demand in connection with the marriage, which attracts the ingredients of Section 498(A) of IPC and Section 4 of the D.P Act.
33.
The death of Chandini has taken place within 7 years from the date of marriage, under suspicious circumstances.
There is ample evidence to show that appellant/accused No.1 was very much present in the house when the incident took place.
P.W.8, neighbour has stated that the accused oftenly used to quarrel with the deceased and even on the date of incident, there was a quarrel.
We are convinced that the appellant i.e., accused No.1 was demanding that two acres land should be registered in his name.
There is no other reason - 25 - NC: 2026:KHC-D:1371-DB HC-KAR forthcoming to hold that the deceased sustained burn injuries for any other reason.
There is absolutely no explanation given by the accused as to how the incident took place or for what reason and how the deceased sustained burn injuries.

34. On the other hand, the evidence on record would clearly establish that the accused was demanding dowry and subjecting the deceased to cruelty and even on the date of incident, he quarreled with the deceased.
Hence, presumption under Section 113(B) of the Evidence Act is applicable to the facts of the present case.
The reasons assigned by the trial Court for holding the accused guilty for the offence punishable under Section 498(A), 304(B) of IPC and Section 4 of the D.P., cannot be found fault with.
However, the reasons assigned by the trial Court for convicting and sentencing the accused for the offence punishable under Section 302 of IPC is liable to be set aside.

At this stage, the learned counsel for the appellant submitted that, accused No.2 to 4 were tried in Sessions case No.53/2019 and after a full-fledged trial, the learned Sessions Judge has acquitted them of the charges leveled against them, vide judgment dated 15.02.2023.
The said judgment has become final, as there is no challenge to the same, as on today.
However, the evidence against the appellant/accused No.1 has been independently assessed by us and we have come to the above conclusion.

The Trial Court framed charges under Sections 3 and 4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act, Sections 498(A) and 304(B) of IPC and in the alternative Section 302 R/w 34 of IPC.
If the Trial Court was of the opinion that, it was a case of 302 IPC, based on the evidence and material on the record, then question of convicting the accused again for the offence punishable under Section 304(B) of IPC would not arise.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
Similarly, if there is no evidence to establish the charge under Section 302 IPC, and if there was evidence to show that the deceased was subjected to cruelty for the purpose of dowry soon before her death, the Trial Court would be justified in convicting the accused for the offence under Section 304(B) of IPC.
8.
However, there is no evidence to show that the deceased caught fire and sustained burn injuries due to stove burst.
Hence, we are of the firm view that the deceased sustained burn injuries not accidentally and not on account of stove burst.
The deceased sustained burn injuries under suspicious circumstances and the fact that the accused also sustained burn injuries and his abscondence would establish the charge against him under Section 302 of IPC.

29. Evidence of P.W.8 is not helpful to the prosecution to prove the charge under Section 302 of IPC.
Further, merely because the accused was absconding from the spot after the incident will also not - 22 - NC: 2026:KHC-D:1371-DB HC-KAR lead to draw an inference that he has committed the murder.
The suspicion cannot take the place of proof, however grave.
30.
To prove the charge under Section 4 of D.P. Act, 498(A) and 304(B) of IPC, the prosecution is mainly relying on the evidence of P.Ws.1, 5 to 10.
Even though there was no complaint or case registered for causing burn injuries to the leg of deceased, the said fact has been spoken by the - 24 - NC: 2026:KHC-D:1371-DB HC-KAR witnesses including P.W.7, the Jamath President.
There is nothing elicited in the cross-examination of the witnesses to disbelieve the same.
From the evidence of the above witnesses, we have no hesitation to hold that the appellant/accused No.1, two years after the marriage, was harassing the deceased and subjecting her to cruelty making unlawful demand in connection with the marriage, which attracts the ingredients of Section 498(A) of IPC and Section 4 of the D.P Act.
33.
The death of Chandini has taken place within 7 years from the date of marriage, under suspicious circumstances.
There is ample evidence to show that appellant/accused No.1 was very much present in the house when the incident took place.
There is absolutely no explanation given by the accused as to how the incident took place or for what reason and how the deceased sustained burn injuries.
34. On the other hand, the evidence on record would clearly establish that the accused was demanding dowry and subjecting the deceased to cruelty and even on the date of incident, he quarreled with the deceased.
Hence, presumption under Section 113(B) of the Evidence Act is applicable to the facts of the present case.
The reasons assigned by the trial Court for holding the accused guilty for the offence punishable under Section 498(A), 304(B) of IPC and Section 4 of the D.P., cannot be found fault with.
However, the reasons assigned by the trial Court for convicting and sentencing the accused for the offence punishable under Section 302 of IPC is liable to be set aside.
